about.title: About the fest
body: IBM Qiskit Fall Fest is an annual initiative that brings together thousands of quantum enthusiasts.
This year, it will happen in Astana, Kazakhstan for the first time. Dive into quantum computing, learn about its significant potential, and challenge your skills at the QFFCA’26 Hackathon.

whatYouGet.title: What you get
items: Lectures with an introduction to quantum computing and Qiskit
Access to real IBM quantum computers through the IBM Quantum Platform
Lab tours: Quantum Sensors Lab and Intermediate Physics Lab (Optics)
A week-long hackathon where you can turn what you learn into working projects with Qiskit

items.q: I'm still in school — can I join?
items.a: Yes. The lectures start from the ground up and assume no university coursework. If you can follow along and you're curious, you belong here.

items.q: Do I need a background in physics?
items.a: Yes. To better understand the material: (a) review linear algebra on Khan Academy; (b) watch ?A Beginner?s Guide to Quantum Computing? by Shohini Ghose on YouTube.

items.q: Do I need to know how to program?
items.a: A basic level helps. Week 3 is dedicated to a beginner-friendly guide to programming with Qiskit.
No. You can attend the lectures and lab tours without joining the hackathon.

coc.title: Code of Conduct
coc.lede: Qiskit Fall Fest Central Asia 2026 is a learning space. Everyone is welcome, and everyone is responsible for keeping it that way.

sections.heading: What we expect
sections.body: Treat every participant, speaker, organizer and member of staff with respect. Assume good faith. Ask before you take someone's photo. Give people room to ask beginner questions — most of the room is a beginner at something.

sections.heading: What is not acceptable
sections.body: Harassment in any form, including comments about gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion or level of experience. Intimidation, stalking, unwelcome photography, sustained disruption of talks, and unwelcome physical contact or attention.

sections.heading: Academic honesty
sections.body: The hackathon is judged on what your team built. Use of libraries, published work and AI tools is fine when you say so. Passing off someone else's work as your own is not.

sections.heading: Consequences
sections.body: Organizers may take any action they consider appropriate, from a warning to removal from the event without a refund of any travel or costs, and exclusion from future events.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: If you experience or witness a breach of this code, contact any organizer on site, or write to us. Reports are handled confidentially.
